hero.title: Urological cancer care
hero.summary: Get clear guidance for prostate, bladder, kidney, testicular, and other urinary cancers. Understand symptoms, tests, treatment options, recovery, and follow-up.

sidebar.ctaText: Share your reports and plan the next step.

body: Urological cancer includes cancers of the prostate, bladder, kidney, testicles, penis, ureter, and other parts of the urinary system. These conditions can feel frightening, but a clear plan makes the journey easier to understand.

The right care depends on the cancer type, stage, grade, scan findings, biopsy report, general health, and personal goals. Dr. Vikram reviews each detail and explains the next step in simple language.

subsections.title: Symptoms
body: Common warning signs include blood in urine, a testicular lump, swelling, side pain, unexplained weight loss, repeated urinary symptoms, weak urine flow, or pain that does not settle.
Some cancers may not cause symptoms early. A scan, PSA test, cystoscopy, biopsy, or routine check may find a problem before symptoms become obvious.

subsections.title: When to consult a urologist
body: Consult a urologist if you notice blood in urine, a testicular lump, repeated urinary symptoms, abnormal PSA, a kidney mass on scan, or a biopsy report that needs review.
You should also seek review if you have been advised surgery, want a second opinion, or need help understanding cancer stage and treatment choices.

subsections.title: Diagnosis and tests
body: Tests may include urine tests, blood tests, PSA, ultrasound, CT, MRI, PET scan, cystoscopy, biopsy, pathology review, and tumor markers when needed.
The aim is to confirm the cancer type, stage, grade, spread, and fitness for treatment before making a decision.

experience.title: Treatment options for urological cancer
body: Cancer treatment is not the same for every patient. Some people need close monitoring. Some need surgery. Some need combined care with oncology.
Dr. Vikram explains what each option means, what recovery may look like, and how follow-up will be planned.
experience.featureText: Care is planned around cancer type, stage, biopsy report, scan findings, overall health, and patient preference.

video.title: "Every patient should understand the diagnosis, the options, and the reason behind the treatment plan."

careGuide.title: Before, during, and after cancer care
careGuide.intro: Cancer care works best when reports are complete and follow-up is planned from the start.

tabs.label: Before Treatment
items: Bring all scans, biopsy reports, and blood tests
Ask what stage and grade mean
Share all medicines and health conditions
Arrange family support if treatment is planned
Keep a folder of all reports

tabs.label: During Treatment
items: Ask about urine catheter or stent if relevant

tabs.label: After Treatment
items: Review final pathology if surgery was done
Report blood in urine, fever, pain, or swelling
Keep all reports for future comparison

careGuide.note: Your exact instructions will depend on cancer type, stage, treatment plan, and general health.

items.question: Does blood in urine always mean cancer?
items.answer: No. It can happen due to infection, stones, prostate issues, or other causes. It still needs proper evaluation.

items.question: Should I get a second opinion?
items.answer: A second opinion can help you understand the diagnosis, stage, and treatment choices before making a decision.

items.question: Is robotic surgery always needed?
items.answer: No. Robotic surgery is useful for selected cases. The right option depends on cancer type, stage, and patient fitness.

items.question: How long is recovery after cancer surgery?
items.answer: Recovery depends on the organ, procedure, and overall health. The team will explain hospital stay, catheter care, activity, and follow-up.

items.question: How often will follow-up be needed?
items.answer: Follow-up depends on cancer type and stage. It may include scans, blood tests, urine tests, cystoscopy, or PSA checks.
